title: Pseudo-Brand Cart Filter
oneLiner: Amazon shoppers and deal curators separate real brands from keyword-stuffed pseudo-brands before checkout regret.
theme: marketplace trust, pseudo-brand filtering, checkout regret prevention
targetUser: Amazon shoppers, deal newsletter writers, marketplace curators, family tech buyers, and consumer-rights content creators overwhelmed by pseudo-brand listings.
keyUX: Paste product listings, score brand legitimacy, compare seller clues, show review and naming red flags, and export a safer shortlist before buying.
sourceSignalReferences: S14 GitHub fresh top repos include scroll-world, knockoff, T3MP3ST, grok-build, and local-llm
S6 Restaurant owners report price-sensitive middle-income customers, haggling, and free-food demands
stitchPrompt: Build a production-grade web prototype called "Pseudo-Brand Cart Filter" for Amazon shoppers and deal curators avoiding keyword-stuffed pseudo-brands. The first screen must be a working cart review surface with listing paste tray, brand legitimacy score, seller clue table, review-pattern warning lane, price-vs-trust comparator, known-brand alternative rail, and shareable cart verdict. Use realistic sample data: charger, kitchen tool, three odd brand names, one established brand, review spikes, coupon badges, and delivery dates. Design direction: use the calm-consumer profile with reassuring comparison cards, soft but not beige-heavy neutrals, one trustworthy green-blue action accent, plain-language warnings, and mobile-friendly decision steps.
